line: In Jung's sources water is the permanent water that is also quicksilver, a living substance, and the unconscious.

sections.title: The permanent water
sections.line: The water of the work is both the stone and its solvent, and the aqua permanens is the alchemical counterpart of the water of life.

quotes.quote: This account makes one thing very evident: the philosophical water is the stone or the prima materia itself; but at the same time, it is also its solvent
Therefore in alchemy Mercurius is sometimes a “spirit” and sometimes a “water,” the so-called aqua permanens, which is none other than argentum vivum.
The water of life has its parallel in the aqua permanens of alchemy.
There can be no doubt that this is the aqua permanens or aqua pontica, the primal water which contains the four elements.

sections.title: Living and dissolving
sections.line: The alchemists call the water a living substance that kills and vivifies, and dissolves the body into spirit.

quotes.quote: They called it aqua nostra, mercurius vivus, argentum vivum, vinum ardens, aqua vitae, succus lunariae, and so on, by which they meant a living being not devoid of substance, as opposed to the rigid immateriality of mind in the abstract.
But of the aqua permanens it was said: “It kills and vivifies.”
The “Gloria mundi” says: “The mystery of every thing is life, which is water; for water dissolves the body into spirit and summons a spirit from the dead.”

sections.title: The unconscious
sections.line: Jung reads the chaotic water as the unconscious, as a large expanse of water signifies it in dreams, and the mother as its source.

quotes.quote: which the old writers could grasp only in projected form, just as today most people cannot see the beam in their own eye
In dreams and fantasies the sea or a large expanse of water signifies the unconscious.
Just as the father represents collective consciousness, the traditional spirit, so the mother stands for the collective unconscious, the source of the water of life

sections.title: Water and spirit
sections.line: In the alchemical language water and spirit are often the same, and water comes from spirit in the numbered sequence of generation.

quotes.quote: Water and spirit are often identical.
The water is a soul or spirit, that is, a psychic “substance,” which now in its turn is applied to the initial material.
1: the spirit of the Living God; 2: spirit from spirit; 3: water from spirit; 4: fire from water;
quotes.voice: Numbers as quoted from a source by Jung

quotes.quote: as they are in the language of the early Christians, for whom water meant the spiritus veritatis.
